basis: The printing heads this quaestio 'VERS. 6.' and it opens '(Cap. XVIII.—Vers. 6.) Et dixit ei: Festina, tres mensuras farinae similae commisce. Quia'. Migne prints the chapter at the head of this block.
date_basis: Written at Bethlehem and named in Jerome's own De viris illustribus 135, finished in 393, among the works already published; the preface announces it as the first of a series of Hebrew Questions on the whole of Scripture that he never continued. The early 390s is as close as the evidence held here reaches. The date is the writing, not the 1845 printing and not Vallarsi's 1767 edition.
text: (Cap. XVIII.—Vers. 6.) Et dixit ei: Festina, tres mensuras farinae similae commisce. Quia tres mensurae absolute hic dictae videntur, et est incerta mensura: propterea addidi, quod in Hebraeo tria sata habeat, id est tres amphoras: ut idem mysterium et hic, et in Evangelio, ubi mulier tria sata farinae fermentare dicitur, cognoscamus (Matth. XIII, 33).
